# Typewell

> A rich-text notes app that is one HTML file. It runs entirely in the browser,
> keeps notes in localStorage, needs no account and no server, and can
> optionally back up to a folder of .md files in your own Google Drive or to a
> secret GitHub Gist.

Free, no sign-up, no tracking, no analytics. Open source under the MIT licence.
Works offline once loaded. Source: https://github.com/aronbraun/typewell

## Pages

- [Typewell](https://typewell.net/): the app itself, and the only page with content — features, keyboard shortcuts and the "how it works" text all live inside it.
- [Privacy](https://typewell.net/privacy.html): what is stored, where, and under which localStorage keys. Nothing leaves the browser unless you connect Drive or a Gist.
- [Terms](https://typewell.net/terms.html): the licence and the disclaimer.

## What it does

- Headings, bold/italic/underline, text and highlight colours, font size and family
- Bulleted, numbered and task lists, with drag handles and nesting
- Tables, code blocks, blockquotes, callouts, links, horizontal rules
- Images you can resize by dragging, and place inline, left, centred, right, or
  with the text wrapping around them; a small one moves inline by itself unless
  you have picked a placement for it
- Multiple notes, search, word and character counts, caret position
- Four themes: white, paper (default), dark, navy
- Adjustable page width: narrow, normal, wide, full width, or an exact
  number of pixels
- Export and import as Markdown or HTML
- Share one note as a read-only link, from a Share button on the top bar: the
  note is compressed into the URL fragment, so nothing is uploaded and no server
  ever sees it. Embedded pictures travel too, re-encoded smaller for the link
- Reopens the note you were last reading, not the first one in the list
- Optional sync: a folder of .md files in your Google Drive (drive.file scope
  only — it can only see files it created), or a secret Gist

## Notes for crawlers

The evidence as of 2026 is that the AI search crawlers do not read this file —
they read the rendered HTML. It is here because it is cheap and because coding
agents do fetch it. The page itself is plain server-served HTML with the text
in it, so there is nothing here that is not also in the page.
